column1: # Game profile of Super Woden Rally Edge (Switch, base game 1.0.0 = v0). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 6000.3.17f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 21.4.7 (NPLN, gRPC); subsdk0 is the movie module (H.264 movies through VideoToolbox). No bundles: the Shader and ComputeShader objects are in
# the player's serialized files (Data/*.assets, level*, Data/Resources), which have no type trees, so unityfs.py carries Unity 6000.3's layouts (SHADER_6000_3, COMPUTE_6000_3).
# Docked: the game draws 1440x810 into 1920x1080 window textures and sets the window crop to 1440x810, paced by the vsync event at 60 fps

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true, and main never sets a heap: Unity 6 takes its memory itself through nn::os::AllocateAddressRegion
# and AllocateMemoryPages in the alias region, as in Hollow Knight: Silksong. The 5 GB block of the other Unity games with virtual address memory, with the node area cut for this sdk build
# (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py). Measured on the Mac over the menus and the first stage: the alias region's high-water mark +2.01 GB of 4.375 GB, 1.24 GB mapped, resident 1.8-2.0 GB and
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything is under Data/: 384 Shader and 21 ComputeShader objects (12,833 stage shaders, 11 of them GLSLC outputs of Unity's player in main)
